reason.en: No genuine market investment can promise returns without risk. Such promises are commonly used to make a person send money quickly.

citation.label: SEBI investor warnings on guaranteed returns

action.en: Do not send money; verify the person and service through the official SEBI website.

reason.en: A claim of profit with no chance of loss is not normal market language. It can hide a fraudulent scheme or an unregistered service.

citation.label: SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003

action.en: Treat the claim as unsafe and do not act until an independent official check is complete.

reason.en: SEBI registration does not mean that SEBI guarantees returns or approves a private profit promise. Fraudsters misuse SEBI's name to create trust.

citation.label: SEBI investor guidance on registration and approval claims

action.en: Check the exact entity name and registration details on SEBI's official intermediary search.

reason.en: Anyone can type 'SEBI registered' in a message. The claim is not proof; scammers copy or invent registration details to look trustworthy. A real registration must be checked by exact name and number.

citation.label: SEBI intermediary registration — verify on SEBI's official register

action.en: Verify the exact name and registration number on SEBI's official website before trusting the claim.

reason.en: A number shown in a message may be copied, altered, or linked to another entity. A number alone does not prove that the sender is genuine.

citation.label: SEBI intermediary registration and verification mechanism

action.en: Search the number and legal name independently on the official SEBI website, without using the message link.

reason.en: Fraudsters may use exchange names or logos to appear legitimate. Exchange membership must be checked through the exchange's official directory.

citation.label: NSE and BSE authorised member verification mechanisms

action.en: Verify the member or intermediary directly on the official exchange website.

keywords: speaking on behalf of your adviser

reason.en: Scammers copy the name, logo, photographs, or registration details of a real adviser. The real firm may have no connection with the message.

citation.label: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013

action.en: Call the adviser using contact details from its official website or SEBI record.

reason.en: A fake application can show false balances and capture passwords or money. A familiar logo does not prove that the application is genuine.

citation.label: SEBI investor alerts on fake trading applications

action.en: Use only the application store link published on your broker's verified official website.

reason.en: A copied website may collect login details while looking like a real broker. Small changes in the domain name can be hard to notice on a phone.

citation.label: SEBI and CERT-In phishing safety guidance

action.en: Close the link and type the broker's known website address yourself.

reason.en: An APK sent through chat can contain malware and may bypass store safety checks. It can steal banking details or control the phone.

citation.label: RBI advisory on mobile and digital payment security

action.en: Do not install the file; delete it and scan the phone with trusted security tools.

reason.en: IPO allotments follow formal application and registrar processes. A message demanding money for a guaranteed allotment is a strong fraud warning.

citation.label: SEBI public issue and IPO application framework

action.en: Check the application and allotment only through the recognised exchange, registrar, or bank channel.

reason.en: A private message cannot reserve or guarantee SME IPO shares. Fraudsters often use unfamiliar company names to demand advance payments.

citation.label: SEBI public issue framework for SME platforms

action.en: Verify the issue on the official exchange and never pay a personal account for allotment.

reason.en: Grey-market dealings may lack normal investor protections and can involve false allotment claims. A guaranteed pre-IPO gain is especially unsafe.

citation.label: SEBI investor cautions on unregulated securities offers

action.en: Do not transfer money for an informal pre-IPO offer; use only regulated public issue channels.

reason.en: Promoters may spread excitement to push up a thinly traded share and then sell. A sudden tip about a little-known company needs strong caution.

citation.label: SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003

action.en: Do not trade from the message; save the evidence and verify the information from official disclosures.

reason.en: Private tip groups can hide the identity and history of the person making the claims. Paid access does not prove registration or accuracy.

citation.label: SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014

action.en: Do not pay for access until the provider's registration and identity are independently verified.

reason.en: Fraudsters use small urgent fees to test whether a person will keep paying. More fees often follow after the first transfer.

citation.label: RBI digital payment fraud awareness guidance

action.en: Stop the payment and contact the bank through its official customer-care channel.

reason.en: A membership label can make a risky offer look exclusive and trustworthy. It does not establish that the provider is regulated.

citation.label: SEBI investor education on unregistered investment advice

action.en: Verify the provider's registration before sharing money or personal details.

reason.en: Screenshots can be edited or taken from another account. They do not prove that the platform is genuine or that money can be withdrawn.

citation.label: SEBI investor caution on testimonials and performance claims

action.en: Treat screenshots as unverified evidence and do not transfer money because of them.

reason.en: Testimonials may be paid, copied, or completely false. A story about someone else's result cannot establish safety.

citation.label: SEBI advertising and investor-protection principles

action.en: Ask for independently verifiable records instead of relying on testimonials.

reason.en: A personal UPI ID may send money to an individual instead of a regulated business. Recovery can be difficult after the transfer.

citation.label: RBI digital payment safety guidance

action.en: Do not pay; verify the beneficiary name in the payment screen and use only official payment routes.

reason.en: Investment money should not normally be sent to an unrelated person's savings account. This is a common way to move scam proceeds.

citation.label: RBI customer-protection and digital payment fraud guidance

action.en: Stop the transfer and confirm the beneficiary with the regulated institution using an official number.

reason.en: A person claiming to release a refund may demand another payment first. Official complaint or refund processes do not make an unknown caller trustworthy.

citation.label: SCORES — SEBI complaint redress

action.en: Do not pay the caller; contact the original institution through its official website.

reason.en: After a loss, scammers may promise recovery and request fees or account access. This can create a second loss.

citation.label: National Cyber Crime helpline 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in

action.en: Do not pay a recovery agent; report the original fraud promptly through 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

reason.en: Search results and social messages can display fake support numbers. A caller may ask for OTPs, remote access, or a transfer.

citation.label: RBI customer-care and digital payment safety guidance

action.en: Find customer care only inside the official app, bank statement, or verified website.

reason.en: Police, SEBI, or courts do not conduct a digital arrest through a threatening video call. Scammers use fear to force immediate payments.

citation.label: Indian cybercrime advisories on digital arrest scams

action.en: End the call, do not transfer money, and report the incident to 1930 or the nearest police station.

reason.en: Dabba trading records bets outside recognised exchanges and removes normal investor protections. The operator can refuse withdrawals or disappear.

citation.label: SEBI warnings on illegal dabba trading

action.en: Do not open the account; use only a verified broker connected to a recognised exchange.

reason.en: A platform outside the regulated system may show invented prices or balances. It may provide no reliable complaint or recovery route.

citation.label: SEBI intermediary registration framework

action.en: Check the broker in the official exchange and SEBI directories before registering.

reason.en: Money-doubling claims hide high risk and may involve unauthorised platforms or payment routes. A foreign-exchange label does not make a scheme legal.

citation.label: RBI foreign exchange and unauthorised electronic trading platform advisories

action.en: Do not deposit funds; check whether the entity is authorised by the relevant Indian regulator.

reason.en: Doubling schemes commonly use fake wallets or social accounts and cannot guarantee repayment. Crypto transfers are often difficult to reverse.

citation.label: Indian cybercrime advisories on cryptocurrency investment scams

action.en: Do not send crypto or money; preserve the wallet address and report suspected fraud.

reason.en: A fake job may show small early rewards and then demand larger deposits to unlock tasks. Employment should not require investment payments.

citation.label: National Cyber Crime advisories on task-based fraud

action.en: Do not deposit money for a job; block the contact and report any payment fraud quickly.

reason.en: A face or voice in a video can be copied or generated. Public figures may have no connection with the account or offer.

citation.label: SEBI investor warnings on impersonation and social-media fraud

action.en: Verify the post on the person's official verified account and do not use a private payment link.

reason.en: Borrowing increases pressure because the loan must be repaid even if the investment loses value. Fraudsters use this pressure to increase the amount sent.

citation.label: SEBI investor education on risk and leverage

action.en: Pause and do not borrow or pledge assets because of a message or caller.

reason.en: Remote-access tools can let another person see or control the phone. They may observe OTPs, banking screens, or payment authorisations.

citation.label: RBI advisory on remote-access and screen-sharing applications

action.en: Never install remote-access software for an unknown caller; uninstall it and contact your bank if it was used.

reason.en: Banks, brokers, exchanges, and regulators do not need your OTP, PIN, password, or CVV to give support. Sharing them can allow unauthorised access.

citation.label: RBI never-share OTP, PIN, password, and CVV guidance

action.en: Do not share the credential; change it immediately if it was already disclosed.

reason.en: A shared screen can reveal account numbers, OTPs, PIN entry, or private messages. A support person does not need to watch your entire screen.

citation.label: RBI digital banking safety guidance

action.en: Refuse the request and close the call or chat.

reason.en: A shortened link hides the real website and can lead to phishing or malware. It is difficult to check the destination before opening it.

citation.label: CERT-In phishing and malicious-link safety guidance

action.en: Do not open the short link; find the organisation's website independently.

reason.en: A lookalike or punycode domain can resemble a trusted name while being controlled by someone else. The spelling may be hard to notice on a small screen.

citation.label: CERT-In domain and phishing safety guidance

action.en: Do not log in; use a saved official bookmark or manually typed domain.

reason.en: Scammers create fear that an account will be blocked and then collect identity or banking details. Genuine KYC updates should use the institution's known channel.

citation.label: RBI KYC fraud advisories and customer-protection guidance

action.en: Ignore the message link and check KYC status inside the official bank or broker application.

reason.en: The speaker may earn money when you click, join, or deposit. Promotional content is not independent investor education.

citation.label: SEBI guidance on advertising and disclosure by investment-related persons

action.en: Check whether the speaker clearly discloses the commercial relationship before taking any action.

reason.en: Moving a financial offer to private chat reduces visibility and makes checking the claims harder. It can also enable pressure and repeated requests for money.

citation.label: SEBI social-media investor-protection guidance

action.en: Keep communication in a verifiable official channel and do not share personal documents in private chat.

reason.en: Absolute words hide uncertainty and can be used to sell a tip. Markets cannot be described honestly as certain.

citation.label: SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014

action.en: Treat the claim as promotional and seek independently verified information.

reason.en: A serious financial communication should explain that value can fall and losses are possible. Omitting risk can create a misleading impression.

citation.label: SEBI advertising code and investor-risk disclosure principles

action.en: Pause and look for clear risk information from an authorised source.

reason.en: Registration identifies a regulated role; it does not guarantee performance or protect every transaction. Fraudsters use the word as a sales shortcut.

citation.label: SEBI intermediary registration and investor-protection guidance

action.en: Verify both the registration and the exact service being offered.

reason.en: Popularity does not prove safety or legality. Fraudsters use group success stories to reduce careful checking.

citation.label: SEBI investor education on behavioural risks

action.en: Make no payment until you have checked the entity and offer independently.

reason.en: Urgency prevents a person from checking registration, beneficiary details, and complaints. A genuine service should allow time for verification.

citation.label: SEBI investor-protection guidance on pressure tactics

action.en: Stop and wait; verify the offer through an independent official source.

reason.en: Scarcity claims can make a person act before checking facts. They are especially suspicious when linked to a private payment.

citation.label: SEBI investor education on misleading solicitations

action.en: Ignore the deadline and verify whether the opportunity exists through official records.

reason.en: A demand for secrecy stops family members or bank staff from spotting warning signs. Trustworthy financial services do not need secret payments.

citation.label: SEBI and cybercrime fraud-prevention guidance

action.en: Discuss the message with a trusted person before taking any step.

reason.en: Threats are used to make people act without checking who is calling. Regulators and banks have formal processes and do not demand secret transfers under threats.

citation.label: Indian cybercrime advisories on impersonation and extortion

action.en: End the conversation and contact the named organisation through its official channel.

reason.en: Fast-rich claims target hopes and hide the possibility of loss. They often lead to repeated deposits or referrals.

citation.label: SEBI investor education on unrealistic return claims

action.en: Do not send money based on a fast-wealth promise; verify the entity first.

reason.en: Refusing verification is a warning sign because legitimate providers can explain their identity and process. Pressure removes the user's chance to make a safe decision.

citation.label: SEBI investor-protection and intermediary-verification guidance

action.en: Pause the transaction until identity, registration, and beneficiary details are checked independently.
